name: ANB Capital
legal_name: ANB Capital Company (a Saudi Closed Joint Stock Company, Single Person Company); formerly Arab National Investment Company
founded: 2007 registration (CR 1010239908 dated 7 Nov 2007; CMA resolution 2007-36-4 dated 5 Jul 2007; CMA licence 07072-37). Commercial operations began 12 Jan 2008 when it took over ANB's investment services and asset management activities. Renamed from Arab National Investment Company to ANB Capital Company on 29 Jun 2022 (same CR).
ownership_summary: Wholly owned by Arab National Bank (100,000,000 shares of SAR 10; 100% at 31 Dec 2024 and 31 Dec 2025). Share capital SAR 1,000m, fully paid (raised from SAR 400m to SAR 1,000m in March 2017). The annual report calls it the bank's 'sole investment arm'. No dividends were declared or paid in 2024 or 2025.
government_link: Indirect at most. The parent, Arab National Bank, is 40% owned by Arab Bank PLC (Jordan), with no government holder above 5% disclosed (see sa-anb). Nothing government-owned at anb capital level.
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of Arab National Bank (sa-anb), fully consolidated by the parent. No subsidiaries other than special purpose vehicles that hold fund assets under CMA rules; these SPVs are not consolidated (AR 2025). Holds a 23.76% associate stake in the Sara Second Real Estate Investment Fund (SAR 325m invested 21 May 2020, equity accounted). Double counting: the parent reports anb capital as its 'Investment and brokerage services' segment (see sa-anb, where the segment total is within SAR 0.2m of anb capital's own SAR 556.2m operating income). Never add this record's figures to sa-anb. Roughly a third of anb capital's own FY2025 operating income came from the parent (SAR 175.9m of SAR 556.2m, calculated from note 17: deposit commission 150.4m, advisory fee 10.0m, discretionary portfolio fees 10.3m, corporate finance 4.3m, custody 0.9m).
footprint: Saudi Arabia only. Head office King Faisal Road, Murabbaa, Riyadh. Four investment centres on the website (checked 12 Oct 2026): Riyadh (2), Al-Khobar, Jeddah. International brokerage reaches GCC, Egypt and US markets through the anb capital Global platform. Also distributes funds through the anb mobile app (parent).
customer_segments: Individual investors (retail, HNW; wealth management for 'individuals, families, entrepreneurs and corporations'); discretionary mandates for corporate, institutional and HNW clients with investable assets of SAR 20m or more; institutional clients served by a dedicated sales team (asset managers, sovereign wealth funds, family offices); corporates and government entities for investment banking; anb retail and affluent clients via the parent.
business_lines: FY2025 operating income SAR 556.2m (audited): asset management fees 181.1m; special commission on cash deposits 150.4m (all placed with the parent); margin lending income 96.0m; investment banking and advisory fees 74.8m; brokerage fees net of Tadawul fees 36.4m; investment gains and other 17.4m. Activities: public mutual funds (14 listed on the website), discretionary portfolio management, 24 closed-ended real estate funds, 4 private equity and venture funds, private fixed income funds, wealth management and advisory, Saudi and international brokerage with Shariah and conventional margin lending, investment banking (ECM, DCM, M&A, debt advisory), sell-side research (since late 2024), and a licence for custody that is not a core activity.

capabilities.wealth_summary: anb capital is the parent bank's sole investment arm and the product engine behind its affluent and private offers (see sa-anb). It reported SAR 24.6bn AUM on a net asset value basis (SAR 28.0bn gross) at 31 Dec 2025. FY2025 operating income was SAR 556.2m, of which asset management fees were SAR 181.1m, margin lending SAR 96.0m, investment banking SAR 74.8m and net brokerage only SAR 36.4m (-22%); SAR 150.4m was interest on deposits placed with the parent. The shelf is 14 public mutual funds (12 Shariah-compliant; Saudi equity, money market, multi-asset and a sovereign sukuk fund), 24 closed-ended real estate funds, 4 private equity and venture funds, private fixed income funds and discretionary mandates from SAR 20m. The Wealth Management page describes research-led advisory and customised portfolios, but publishes no minimums, products or named team beyond the head of the unit. Clients trade Saudi equities in a new app (2025) that has scheduled recurring orders and margin, and international markets (GCC, Egypt, US with fractional shares from USD 1) on the 'anb capital Global' platform, which the site says is powered by Global Trading Network (GTN). 2026 priorities in the annual report: diversify products, grow discretionary mandates, execute a private credit strategy, build joint ventures and partnerships, introduce REITs.

segments.name: Discretionary portfolio management

segments.name: Wealth Management
segments.eligibility: Not published. Targets 'individuals, families, entrepreneurs, and corporations'; no minimums or eligibility criteria stated.

private_banking.detail: anb capital has no private banking unit of its own. Wealth Management (advisory and portfolio management) and discretionary mandates from SAR 20m are the closest services. The parent bank runs Private Banking and the anb Elite proposition (see sa-anb).

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 24.6bn NAV / SAR 28.0bn gross at 31 Dec 2025. 14 public mutual funds on the website (8 equity, 2 money market, 3 multi-asset, 1 sovereign sukuk fund; 12 Shariah, 2 conventional; SAR and USD money market funds). 24 closed-ended real estate funds, 4 private equity and venture funds (anb Seed Fund, healthcare fund), 2 private fixed income funds and 2 public multi-asset funds launched in 2025. Asset management fees SAR 181.1m in FY2025 (+43%). No fund-level AUM published on the website.

brokerage.detail: Saudi Exchange plus GCC (Qatar, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Muscat, Bahrain), Egypt and US exchanges (NYSE, Nasdaq, OTC; options data). Channels: broker-assisted Central Trading Unit, IVR self-trading, web, apps and a TWS active-trader program. Brokerage value traded SAR 68bn in 2025; brokerage fees SAR 36.4m net of Tadawul fees; Shariah and conventional margin lending (SAR 96.0m income). Institutional sales and trading desk with two new global broker relationships in 2025 (brokers not named). Sell-side research since late 2024.

digital_investing.detail: New anb capital trading app and web platform (2025): conditional and stop-loss orders, digital IPO subscriptions, online margin, scheduled recurring investment orders, watchlists (Shariah, newly listed, growth, ESG), analyst ratings, one-tap switch to the global platform. 'anb capital Global' (e-brokerage for GCC, Egypt, US; web, iOS, Android) is stated to be powered by GTN; fractional US shares from USD 1; open to anb capital clients with a local portfolio and an active anb current account. Funds can also be subscribed in the anb mobile app (parent). Launch date of the new app not stated on the page.

advisory.detail: Wealth Management page: research-based investment advisory and customised portfolios, including Shariah-compliant strategies, 'experienced advisors' (not named). Head of Wealth Management since 2022. Investment banking advisory (ECM, DCM, M&A, debt advisory) is a separate division.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management for clients with investable assets of SAR 20m and above; process covers objectives, risk tolerance, execution, periodic review and rebalancing. The parent also places a discretionary portfolio with anb capital (SAR 10.3m fee income in FY2025). 2026 priority: 'Grow DPMs'. DPM AUM not disclosed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found on the anb capital website or in AR 2025. The new app offers scheduled recurring orders (automated investing) and three Shariah multi-asset funds (conservative, balanced, growth) act as risk-profiled options.

funds_platform.detail: Own funds only on the website and in the anb app. No third-party fund shelf or fund-platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: No structured products on the anb capital website or in AR 2025. The parent bank's Treasury sells structured deposits (see sa-anb).

private_markets.detail: 24 closed-ended real estate funds (7 launched in 2025; Narjis View Fund exited at 2.3x cash-on-cash and over 50% IRR); 4 private equity and venture funds including the anb Seed Fund (10 fintech investments) and a healthcare fund (Baraya Extended Care); real estate debt structuring; 2026 priorities include a private credit strategy and expanding VC and PE. Two real estate funds bought land in Al Khobar for over SAR 800m on 30 Jul 2026.

islamic_wealth.detail: 12 of the 14 public funds are labelled Shariah-compliant (Shariah equity, SAR and USD Trade money market, multi-asset and sovereign sukuk funds); Shariah margin lending; Business Gate Fund is Shariah-compliant; annual Shariah Committee report (Arabic) published. The firm offers both Shariah and conventional services.

partners.what: anb capital's Global platform page states it is powered by GTN as technology and market data provider; the Android package ID is com.directfn.mobile.anb_prod. Covers GCC, Egypt and US markets. No announcement or date found.
AR 2025: 'two new global broker relationships' expanded the institutional desk's ability to serve international clients

Funds can be subscribed in the anb mobile app; the bank supplies the margin lending facility (since 1 Apr 2017), holds anb capital's cash deposits (SAR 553.8m current accounts) and places a discretionary portfolio
Named developer and unitholder (about 10%) of a planned SAR 2.1bn real estate fund east of Riyadh; the website lists the 'anbc Riyadh Real Estate Development Fund' (2024, SAR 2,106m).

initiatives.what: Launched an upgraded trading application and web platform: conditional orders, stop-loss tools, digital IPO subscriptions and enhanced online margin trading

Launched 7 closed-ended real estate funds (24 active); introduced two private fixed income funds and two public multi-asset funds; launched a healthcare private equity fund; anb Seed Fund invested in ten fintech companies; full exit of the Narjis View Fund
Investment banking: joint bookrunner on the SAR 4.1bn Flynas IPO and on ANB's SAR 3.3bn and USD 750m Additional Tier 1 issues; investment banking fees +65%
Institutional sales and trading desk added two global broker relationships; sell-side research broadened coverage (insurance, software and services, car rental, retail pharmacies, travel and tourism)
Board reconstituted: three directors resigned (including the parent's wholesale bank head and its head of strategic investments) and three joined (Ziyad Alhazzani, Mashaal Aljomaih, Khaled Alrashed)

2026 priorities (AR 2025): expand AUM under current offerings, diversify products, grow DPMs, execute a private credit strategy, build joint ventures and partnerships with key players, expand VC and grow PE funds, introduce REITs, upgrade the trading platform for regional and global markets, enhance the institutional desk
Two anb capital real estate funds acquired 1.7 million sqm of raw land on King Khalid Road, Al Khobar, for more than SAR 800m
Announced changes to the board memberships of several anb capital funds (fund-governance notice; detail not opened)

opportunities: AR 2025 lists 2026 priorities to 'Diversify our product offering', 'Grow DPMs', 'Execute private credit strategy' and 'Build joint ventures and partnerships with key players' (S4 PDF p.19)
The public fund range is 14 funds, mostly Saudi equity (8 equity, 2 money market, 3 multi-asset, 1 sukuk); no global, third-party or structured products are listed (S7)
Wealth Management page offers advisory and customised portfolios but publishes no minimums, products or platform; the unit is led by a named head since 2022 (S13, S1)
Brokerage is weak: net brokerage income fell 22% to SAR 36.4m in FY2025 while asset management fees rose 43% to SAR 181.1m (S5 PDF p.6)
The new app offers scheduled recurring orders but no robo or model-portfolio product was found (S12)
Plans a 2026 upgrade of the trading platform for regional and global markets and enhanced institutional desk (S4 PDF p.19)
barriers: Captive investment arm: the AR calls it the bank's 'sole investment arm'; SAR 175.9m of FY2025 operating income came from the parent (S4 PDF p.13; S5 note 17)
Own-fund shelf and own channels: funds sold through anb capital and the anb app; no third-party shelf found (S7, S6)
Global trading stack already supplied by GTN (S11)
Largely Shariah-labelled public range (12 of 14 funds), so products need Shariah Committee approval (S7, S15)
Small branch footprint (4 centres) and no disclosed client or user numbers, so scale of the digital opportunity cannot be sized (S14)
incumbent_vendors: Global Trading Network (GTN): named by anb capital as technology and market data provider of the Global platform (S11)
Local trading app and TWS program: vendor not named (S10, S12)

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 lists Obaid A. Alrasheed as Vice Chairperson of the board (Non-Executive, appointed February 2021) and so does its interests table; the website's board page (English and Arabic, checked 12 Oct 2026) lists him as 'Member' only and names no vice chair.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the AR title (dated February 2021 appointment) with a note. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: anb capital AR 2025: 'Chief Personal Bank Officer' at ANB. anb capital website: 'CEO of Retail Banking Group at ANB'. The parent's own title is recorded in sa-anb (Chief Retail Bank Officer).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as a board member with the parent role described generically. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: The website footer still prints 'Arab National Investment Company'. The audited FS state the name changed to ANB Capital Company on 29 Jun 2022 with the same CR.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the FS name; old name kept as 'formerly'. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: Arab News (2 Jan 2023) profiled Muneera Al-Dossary as head of asset management at ANB Capital since June 2022. The official page (Oct 2026) lists Khalid S. Al-Deghaither, who says he was promoted to the role in 2023. A search result for her SISCO profile indicates she left in 2023 for Franklin Templeton Saudi Arabia (page not opened).
discrepancies.resolution: Used the official page. Treat any source naming Al-Dossary as stale.

discrepancies.detail: The AR gives the 2025 decline in Saudi market value traded as 30.2% (PDF p.9), 'more than 40%' (CEO letter) and 43% (PDF p.23).
discrepancies.resolution: No market share was calculated from these figures. Unresolved; likely different measures.

discrepancies.field: Senior executives listed (English vs Arabic page)
discrepancies.detail: On 12 Oct 2026 the English leadership page listed nine senior executives (CEO, COO, CFO, CSO, Head of Brokerage, CGRCO, Heads of Private Equity, Investment Banking and Real Estate). The Arabic page checked the same day listed twelve, adding the Head of Asset Management (Khalid S. Al-Deghaither), Head of Wealth Management (Rakan T. Al-Rubayan) and Head of Product and Business Development (Hussam A. Alsurayhi). The prior pass (R5, same date) had recorded all three on the English page. No departure or appointment news found (English and Arabic role-based searches).
discrepancies.resolution: The three are kept with role_status 'Conflicting sources' and their biographies from the Arabic page. Re-check the English page; confirm before any meeting.

discrepancies.field: Khalid Alghamdi career figures and Mizuho title
discrepancies.detail: Website bio (2026): transactions exceeding USD 100bn including over USD 75bn of IPOs at GIB Capital; 'CEO and Board Member' of Mizuho Saudi Arabia and Credit Suisse Saudi Arabia. AR 2025 and AR 2022: over USD 50bn including over USD 40bn of IPOs; 'Managing Director of Mizuho Saudi Arabia'.
discrepancies.resolution: Both wordings recorded in previous_roles; the annual report (tier 1) is the more conservative figure. Minor.

open_items: No interim standalone statements: anb capital publishes only annual reports and FS (S15). All metrics are FY2025; AUM at 30 Jun 2026 and H1 2026 income are not disclosed. The parent's H1 2026 segment note and investor presentation were not opened because the parent's IR financial-statements page showed 'The Website is under maintenance' on 12 Oct 2026 (S24); the Argaam results page has no segment data (S25). Re-check once the parent publishes Q3 2026 (late Oct 2026).
Clients, brokerage accounts, app users and headcount are not disclosed in any source opened.

The vendor of the local (Saudi) trading app and of the TWS active-trader program is not named. GTN is named only for the Global platform (S11); launch date of the new app is not stated (AR 2025 places it in 2025).
The two 'new global broker relationships' of 2025 are not named.
Wealth Management page gives no eligibility, minimums, product list or team; the wealth unit's balances are not disclosed.

Leads checked: REITs - none launched, only a 2026 priority in AR 2025; robo or model portfolios - not found (recurring orders only); partnerships 2025-2026 - only the GTN platform statement and unnamed brokers; brokerage market share - not disclosed. The lead on digital trading apps is confirmed (new app 2025, Global platform).

The website real estate page lists 22 distinct funds with unlabelled figures (sum about SAR 24.3bn if read as fund sizes); these were not used as AUM and cannot be reconciled to the AR figure of SAR 24.6bn NAV for all assets.

LinkedIn: no profile found for the CEO or the Heads of Wealth Management and Asset Management. LinkedIn matches for Ahab Minhas, Bader Alessa and Omar Ardati are search-result matches only (profiles not opened).

Saudi Exchange fund statement pages (hosted at saudiexchange.sa, seen in search results) and the CMA authorised-person register were not opened. The 25 Aug 2026 fund-board change notice and the 2024 Riyadh Development fund were not followed up.

People pass X17 (12 Oct 2026): the English senior executives page no longer shows the Heads of Asset Management, Wealth Management and Product & Business Development, while the Arabic page still does (S28). Their status is 'Conflicting sources'; confirm whether Al-Deghaither, Al-Rubayan and Alsurayhi remain in post before meetings.

Appointment dates are not published for the Head of Brokerage (current title), Head of Product and Business Development, Head of Real Estate and the Chief GRC Officer; the CEO's 2021 start month is not published; the Chairperson's education is not published in any source opened.

AR 2025 (S4 PDF p.39) discloses that anb capital 'has entered into a contractual agreement' with InvestSky (a fintech in which director Khaled Alrashed holds under 1%); not followed up here — lead for the capabilities/partners pass.

Blocked or unusable in this pass: Saudi Exchange company pages (HTTP 403); the search tool declines name-based LinkedIn look-ups, so no new LinkedIn verification was possible (CEO, Head of Asset Management and Head of Wealth Management remain 'Not verified'). The anb capital LinkedIn company page is linked officially but was not opened.
